tldr: UI-AGILE improves GUI agent grounding through three training-stage RFT enhancements (simple thinking, continuous reward, cropping-based resampling) and one inference-stage method (decomposed grounding with selection), achieving state-of-the-art results on ScreenSpot-Pro and ScreenSpot-v2.
contributions: Simple Thinking strategy that balances reasoning length during training to reconcile the trade-off between grounding accuracy and agent planning ability.
Continuous grounding reward function using Chebyshev distance from the predicted point to the bounding box center, replacing binary reward for precise localization.
Cropping-based resampling strategy that dynamically simplifies difficult training samples by cropping screenshots to mitigate sparse reward during RFT.
Decomposed grounding with selection inference method that breaks high-resolution screenshots into overlapping sub-images, generates candidates, and uses a VLM to select the best match.
methods: The authors propose four methodological contributions built on Qwen2.5-VL, trained on approximately 9K samples for 2 epochs using data from UI-R1, GUI-R1, Aguvis, and Grounding-R1. During training, they (1) apply a 'Simple Thinking' reward function with an ideal reasoning length range using a cosine-shaped non-linear penalty to avoid under-thinking or over-thinking, (2) use a continuous exponential reward based on Chebyshev distance from predicted coordinates to the ground-truth bounding box center for precise localization, and (3) employ cropping-based resampling that scans for valid crops containing the ground-truth bbox when all generations receive zero reward. During inference, they decompose high-resolution screenshots into overlapping sub-images, independently ground each sub-image to collect candidate points, extract element images from candidates, and use a VLM-based Yes/No classifier to adjudicate the best match.
results: On ScreenSpot-Pro, UI-AGILE-7B with decomposed grounding achieves 48.7% average accuracy, a 23% improvement over the best baseline (JEDI-7B). UI-AGILE-3B achieves 45.0% and UI-AGILE-7B achieves 59.2% without decomposed grounding. Decomposed grounding provides plug-and-play improvements across existing models: OS-Atlas-7B improves from 18.9 to 33.1 (+75.1%), Aguvis-7B from 20.4 to 36.5 (+78.9%), and UI-TARS-7B from 35.7 to 41.9. The VLM selection accuracy is approximately 87% (inferred from pass@4 metrics). Models were trained on only ~9K examples for 2 epochs and still surpass RFT baselines like UI-R1-E (33.5%) and GUI-R1-7B (32.1%).
limitations: Trained on a relatively small dataset of approximately 9K samples for only 2 epochs, which may limit generalization.
The decomposed grounding selection stage has imperfect accuracy (~87%), capping overall improvement.
The method requires multiple forward passes during inference, introducing additional overhead despite theoretical computational savings from reduced sequence length in self-attention.
The cropping-based resampling uses a predefined scaling factor that may not be optimal across all task types.
